newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian franc bouncing along ERM midpoint.
newsitem.headline: Belgian franc bouncing along ERM midpoint.

text.p: The Belgian franc bounced along its midpoint to the mark in the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) in late morning trade on Thursday as a scandal in a governing party continued to hurt the currency.
At around 1050 GMT, the franc had weakened to 20.6250/70, the first time it had traded below the midpoint of 20.6255 since May 1995. Late on Wednesday the franc stood at 20.6213/33.

The currency has been weak against the mark for most of the week as Belgium's French-speaking socialist party, the second largest in the country's four-party centre-left governing coalition, has come under pressure from opposition parties to quit power over a widening scandal.

Two senior party figures were charged with corruption on Monday linked to a contract in 1989 to buy air defence systems for the country's F-16 fighter jets from French defence firm Dassault. Dassault has denied all wrongdoing.
In a newspaper interview on Thursday, the opposition French -speaking liberal party offered to replace the socialists.

Belgian foreign exchange traders have said, however, they don't expect the government to collapse, noting the Christian Democrats - the other main governing party - do not want a crisis now as the country prepares for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
A trader at a London bank said 20.6240/50 to the mark was a crucial resistance point for the franc and if it closed weaker than that level today it could move quickly on Friday to 20.63 or beyond.
"It would be a trip much higher (for the mark). It would draw in the U.S. banks," he said.
